questions.enonce_markdown:
Explain briefly the use of the following input technologies and cite a situation in which each can be useful:

(a) Bar code reader. (2 marks)

(b) Optical Character recognition. (2 marks)

(c) Automatic speech recognition. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Bar code reader (2 marks).** A bar code reader (scanner) shines a laser or light beam on a bar code, a pattern of parallel black and white bars of different widths that represents a number (for example an EAN or UPC product code), and measures the reflected light to read the code. The number is sent to the computer, which uses it to look up the record (name, price, stock) in a database without any typing, quickly and with very few errors. *Situation:* a supermarket checkout (the price is found and the stock is updated automatically); also library book loans, luggage handling at an airport and stock control in a warehouse.

**(b) Optical Character Recognition, OCR (2 marks).** OCR is software which, with a scanner (or a camera), analyses the image of a printed or typed page and recognises the shapes of the characters by comparing them with stored patterns, converting them into editable text that the computer can store, search and edit, instead of a picture. *Situation:* converting printed documents, old books or forms into word-processor files to save typing; reading the number plates of vehicles; reading cheques and passports.

**(c) Automatic Speech Recognition, ASR (2 marks).** ASR uses a microphone and software which analyses the sound of the spoken words, compares them with stored sound patterns and a vocabulary, and converts them into text or into commands for the computer; it is more accurate when the software has been trained to the voice of the user. *Situation:* dictating a letter or a report for a person who cannot type or has a disability; hands-free control in a car (voice commands) or on a smartphone (voice assistants); automated telephone services in call centres.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) Differentiate between data integrity and data verification. (2 marks)

(b) Name and describe TWO data verification techniques. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Data integrity and data verification (2 marks).**

- **Data integrity** is the accuracy, completeness and consistency of the data over its whole life in the system: the data stay correct, are not accidentally or deliberately altered or lost, and remain the same in all the places where they are stored. It is maintained by validation checks, access control, back-ups and database constraints (such as keys).
- **Data verification** is the checking that the data entered into the computer (or copied from one medium to another) are the same as the original source, that is, that no error was made during data entry or transmission. It checks the *accuracy of the copying*, not whether the data are sensible (this is validation).

**(b) Two verification techniques (2 marks, 1 mark each).**

1. **Double entry:** the same data are keyed in twice, by the same or by two different operators, and the computer compares the two versions; any difference is reported and corrected.
2. **Visual checking (proofreading):** after the entry, the operator reads the data on the screen or in a printout and compares them with the source document; any difference is corrected.

(Other accepted techniques: a check sum or parity check to verify data transmitted between computers, and the re-entry of a password or e-mail address in a "confirm" field.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) Explain TWO functions of a system analyst. (2 marks)

(b) Explain TWO ways a System Analyst can collect information about a system for analysis. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Two functions of a system analyst (2 marks, 1 mark each).** Any two:

- **Investigating and analysing the existing system:** he or she studies how the current system works, finds its problems and decides what the users really need (the user requirements).
- **Designing the new system:** he or she produces the specification and the design of the new system (inputs, outputs, files, processing and procedures), and chooses the hardware and software.
- **Acting as a link (liaison) between the users and the technical staff:** he or she translates the needs of the users, who are not computer experts, into technical specifications for the programmers.
- **Supervising the implementation:** testing, installation, training of the users, documentation and evaluation of the new system.

**(b) Two ways of collecting information (2 marks, 1 mark each).** Any two:

- **Interviews:** the analyst talks face to face with the managers and users and asks questions; it gives detailed answers and allows follow-up questions, but it takes time.
- **Questionnaires:** written questions are given to many people; it is quick and cheap for a large number of users, but the answers are limited and not all the forms are returned.
- **Observation:** the analyst watches the people at work and sees how the system really works, though people may behave differently when they are watched.
- **Examination of documents:** the analyst studies forms, reports, manuals and files that are used in the system.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) Convert the octal number 256 to binary (base 2). (1 mark)

(b) Convert the binary number 11011.11 to decimal (base 10). (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Octal 256 to binary (1 mark).** Each octal digit is replaced by its 3-bit binary equivalent:

| Octal digit | 2 | 5 | 6 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Binary | 010 | 101 | 110 |

So $256_8 = 010\,101\,110_2$, and removing the leading zero,

$$
256_8 = 10101110_2
$$

*Check:* $2 \times 64 + 5 \times 8 + 6 = 174$ and $10101110_2 = 128 + 32 + 8 + 4 + 2 = 174$.

**(b) Binary 11011.11 to decimal (2 marks).** Use the place values: powers of 2 on the left of the binary point ($2^4 \ldots 2^0$) and negative powers on the right ($2^{-1}$, $2^{-2}$).

$$
11011.11_2 = 1\times 2^4 + 1\times 2^3 + 0\times 2^2 + 1\times 2^1 + 1\times 2^0 + 1\times 2^{-1} + 1\times 2^{-2}
$$

$$
= 16 + 8 + 0 + 2 + 1 + 0.5 + 0.25 = 27.75
$$

So $11011.11_2 = 27.75_{10}$.
